persistence_invariants.brief: Each (sku, location) pair is uniquely addressable; no two records share that combination (R3)
Stock levels never go below zero; CHECK(quantity >= 0) enforced at write time (R2)
Every record keeps an unmodifiable created_at timestamp, NOT NULL and immutable after insert (R1)
Every record keeps an unmodifiable created_by actor identifier, NOT NULL and immutable after insert (R1)
Schema migrations are additive and preserve existing inventory records; every iteration maintains backward compatibility (R1)

nfrs.brief: Existing stock data survives every schema migration with no loss; inventory records created before each iteration persist unchanged
Every inventory adjustment keeps an unmodifiable timestamp and actor
Stock levels never go below zero, and never overcommit beyond available quantity; a pick that would overcommit is rejected at write time
Every SKU at every location is uniquely addressable by (sku, location); no two records share that pair; collision is resolved at write time
Integration tests run against the paired Lakebase branch, not a mock or in-memory substitute; CI refuses to merge a PR without real-branch integration tests
The UI is a React + TypeScript single-page application under client/; the backend is a JSON API (boundary returns data, not server-rendered HTML)
Warehouse-floor tablet loads the app once and navigates client-side (home, SKU detail, receipt/pick/adjustment forms) with no full-page reloads
Stock adjustments update the affected row in place (optimistic update, reconciled against server response) rather than re-rendering the page
Validation errors name the offending field, not just 'bad request'
Migrations are additive where possible; old reads keep working during rollout
Stock-level rows missing optional detail (par level, batch, serial) render cleanly with 'not tracked' labels, not null crashes
Barcode-scan interactions feel immediate (perceived response under ~200ms from scan event to UI update)
